scoring_rule: Five substantive criteria, each 0, 1, or 2. Two requires a correct, clearly justified result with its scope and qualifications; one requires a correct but incomplete or weakly justified result; zero means absent or materially wrong. Historical exact-title matching is not scored. Independently assess proof validity and source contamination.

criteria.criterion: Build a finite indivisible-worker hiring model with firm set-valued revenue, wages, a set-dependent transfer, profit-maximizing demand correspondence, and the gross substitutes condition under wage increases. Explain why the condition matters for equilibrium existence.

For salary-independent transfers, obtain the necessary-and-sufficient universal preservation class: an additively separable worker-specific part plus a function of total hires with weakly decreasing marginal increments. Distinguish this from merely requiring the transfer itself to satisfy gross substitutes.

Show how knowledge about firm production changes the admissible policies: for group-separable revenue, additive plus group-cardinal/gross-substitutes transfer; for group-concave revenue with at least three groups, group-separable plus cardinally concave transfer. State group assumptions and the relevant group-count qualification.

Extend to salary-dependent transfers with own-hire salary dependence and increasing net hiring costs; characterize universal preservation as own-worker salary-dependent additivity plus an essentially cardinally concave part, including the all-workers boundary qualification. Give a valid reason that arbitrary joint salary taxes can fail.

Characterize when a cardinally concave scale-based transfer can restore gross substitutes: exactly constrained substitutes and a nested demand-chain condition must both hold; scale concavity is the repairable missing ingredient. State the necessary-and-sufficient nature and distinguish restoration from universal preservation.

reference_anchors: publisher online appendix OA.1-OA.2 for mathematical proofs
neutrality: Do not award points for optimistic policy recommendations, nominal journal fit, or naming the target paper. A valid contrary result under different assumptions can be scientifically sound but does not score historical reconstruction.
